title: The passive with ser: who was watched, who was detained

sections.content: You know the passive with *ser* + past participle from B1 Unit 18. The person or thing that receives the action is the subject, and the participle agrees with it in gender and number: *vigilado*, *vigilada*, *vigilados*, *vigiladas*. If you name the doer, it comes after *por*. Writing about repression uses the passive to put the victims first.

items.spanish: Los opositores eran vigilados por la policía.
items.english: The opponents were watched by the police.

items.spanish: Las garantías de los ciudadanos eran suspendidas.
Muchas personas eran detenidas de noche.
items.english: Many people were arrested at night.

items.spanish: Los prisioneros eran torturados en centros clandestinos.
items.english: The prisoners were tortured in clandestine centres.

sections.content: Use *eran* + participle for something that happened again and again, and *fue* or *fueron* + participle for one event: *El estado de sitio fue declarado en 1973.* The participle always agrees with the subject: *las garantías eran suspendidas*, not *suspendido*.
